chunks: But whosoever gets his ledger in his left hand, will say: 'Would that I were never given my ledger,'

key_terms.بِشِمَالِهِ: In his left hand, indicating a lesser degree of success or acceptance
key_terms.كِتَابُ: Book of deeds, the record of a person's actions
key_terms.لَمْ: A particle of negation for the past, used here to express 'never were given'
key_terms.يَا لَيْتَنِي: A phrase of strong regret or wish, meaning 'Would that I were'

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a person receives their book of deeds in their left hand on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, receiving the book in the left hand signifies a state of humiliation and loss of honor, contrasting with the dignified reception by the righteous. This verse captures the profound psychological torment of the disbelievers as they confront the tangible reality of their failures, wishing for the non-existence of their record to escape the weight of their sins.
